Natural_Language: This part addresses prioritizing sources of supplies and services for use by the Government.

Natural_Language: Definitions as used in this part: AbilityOne Commission, AbilityOne participating nonprofit agencies, Committee, Central nonprofit agency, Government printing, Procurement List, Related supplies.

Natural_Language: Agencies must acquire the following supplies and services using the procedures listed below: (1) Public utility services using Part 41; (2) Government printing and related supplies using Subpart 8.5; (3) Leased motor vehicles - Contact GSA Fleet; (4) Strategic and critical materials (e.g., metals and ores) from inventories exceeding Defense National Stockpile requirements - DLA Strategic Materials (https://www.dla.mil/Strategic-Materials/).

Natural_Language: Unless otherwise required by law or 8.101, agencies must procure services that are on the Procurement List maintained by the Committee, from AbilityOne Participating Nonprofit Agencies in accordance with subpart 8.2. Natural_Language: In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 3905 and Section 637 of Division H of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2005 (Pub. L. 108-447) (18 U.S.C. 4124 note), agencies must- (a) Before purchasing an item of supply listed in the FPI Schedule, conduct market research to determine whether the FPI item is comparable to supplies available from the private sector that best meet the Government's needs in terms of price, quality, and time of delivery. Natural_Language: The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process to obtain commercial supplies and commercial services at prices associated with volume buying. Agencies must use the FSS, in accordance with 8.104. When placing an order under the FSS, agencies must follow the ordering procedures established by GSA and found at subpart 538.71. GSA ordering procedures follow all statutory requirements, including the requirements of section 863 of the Duncan Hunter National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2009, and have been coordinated with the Office of Federal Procurement Policy for consistency with governmentwide acquisition policy.
